Each rewrite is an identity, so correctness telescopes to $N = N^{+} - N^{-}$; all weights are non-negative, hence both components are monotone in the split variables, with the posynomial representation from Proposition~\ref{prop:posynomial_representation}. These identities give $N = N^{+} - N^{-}$; non-negative weights imply monotonicity and Proposition~\ref{prop:posynomial_representation}'s representation. Growth is controlled by the expanded monomial count: a uniform bound suffices, whereas bounded fan-in with unbounded exponents does not.

The block-list construction yields a finite expression, so recursion on its syntax terminates. We prove by structural induction that every compiled expression has non-negative convex, coordinatewise non-decreasing heads on the input orthant and that their difference equals its ordinary evaluation at $x-y$.

Inputs satisfy the invariant by coordinate projection, and constants by their positive/negative split. Sums preserve every property. Signed scaling either rescales both heads by a non-negative coefficient or swaps them before rescaling, proving the scalar-multiple case. For a product, Proposition~\ref{prop:convex_product_pair} supplies exact recovery and convex, monotone composition on non-negative incoming streams. The supported activations satisfy the corresponding scalar pair theorem. Softmax uses Theorem~\ref{thm:softmax_dc_split} on the nonempty allowed-key vector. LayerNorm uses its explicit centering, square, reciprocal, product, and affine construction; its recovered variance is non-negative and its epsilon is positive. Thus every expression constructor preserves the invariant.

Induction over the block list identifies ordinary evaluation of the compiled output expression with the independently specified forward recurrence~\eqref{eq:arbitrary_depth_transformer}. The expression invariant therefore proves~\eqref{eq:transformer_dc_recovery} at every finite depth, including zero, with no activation at the signed affine readout. Finally, the maps $u\mapsto\posneg{u}{\pm}$ have convex components and take values in the orthant. Convex monotone composition proves global convexity of $g,h$, and subtraction recovers $N(u)$.
changes.after:
The block list yields a finite expression, so syntax recursion terminates. Structural induction shows that each compiled expression has non-negative convex, coordinatewise non-decreasing heads on the input orthant, whose difference evaluates the expression at $x-y$.

Coordinate projections and positive/negative constant splits satisfy this invariant. Sums preserve it; signed scaling rescales by a non-negative coefficient, swapping heads for negative scalars. Proposition~\ref{prop:convex_product_pair} handles products by exact recovery and convex, monotone composition on non-negative streams. The scalar pair theorems handle activations; Theorem~\ref{thm:softmax_dc_split} handles the nonempty allowed-key vector. LayerNorm follows its centering, square, reciprocal, product and affine recipe, with non-negative recovered variance and positive epsilon. Thus every constructor preserves the invariant.

Induction over the block list equates ordinary evaluation with the independently specified recurrence~\eqref{eq:arbitrary_depth_transformer}, proving~\eqref{eq:transformer_dc_recovery} at every finite depth, including zero, with an ungated signed affine readout. Finally, $u\mapsto\posneg{u}{\pm}$ has convex components valued in the orthant. Convex monotone composition gives globally convex $g,h$, and subtraction recovers $N(u)$.
